categories.focal-word-cluster: several of the words large models over-use sit close together; one such word alone is ordinary and is not reported
categories.dash-density: a paragraph that holds two em dashes or more
categories.not-only-but: the 'not only X but Y' connective
categories.inverted-contrast: a point made by first denying something nobody said ('it is not X, it is Y')
categories.list-of-three: three-item lists used again and again
categories.even-rhythm: four or more sentences in a row of nearly the same length
categories.stock-opener: an opening that sets a scene any text could have
categories.stock-closer: a closing phrase that announces the summary
categories.bold-lead-bullets: a list whose items each open with a bold label
categories.hedge-stack: two or more hedges on one claim
categories.self-answered-question: a short question answered at once by a fragment

reading: A row is a place to read closely. It is not a fault, and the report is not a score: never judge a text by how many rows it has, and never edit a text to empty it.
